goal: Determine the clearest evidence-backed view system through which a reader can understand the Thin Recursive Work Orchestrator design as a whole and inspect every part without collapsing structure, runtime sequence, state ownership, or authority. Recommend one primary explanatory view architecture, map every design section and ontology cluster into it, and specify a smallest honest implementation-ready view contract without building the view.
context: The candidate DESIGN.md and ONTOLOGY.md define a thin recursive work orchestrator in which leaf and composite work share one Work contract, one root orchestrator expands a composition graph, work units own domain status and confirmation, and a command/event bus plus journal transport and preserve records without deciding or executing work. The design is proposal-only and its runtime is unimplemented. Inventory precedents support removable learner projections, synchronized graph/outline/table views, visible authority boundaries, and strict separation between browser inspectability and human comprehension. Research must test rather than assume the working hypothesis that coordinated Structure, Flow, and Ownership views are clearer than one giant graph. It may recommend a view grammar and acceptance contract, but it cannot edit the design or ontology, build HTML or product code, promote definitions, claim runtime evidence, or claim human comprehension.
anti_bias_global: Formal system anatomy versus causal runtime tracing versus learner-centered progressive disclosure, followed by independent precedent, non-vacuity, and definitional attacks.

groups.anti_bias: Composite methodology and source-corpus axis: formal architecture notation, temporal and causal workflow tracing, and learner-centered coordinated information visualization.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 uses formal structural decomposition over architecture-notation and system-model sources while agent 1 uses temporal causal tracing over workflow, event, state-machine, and observability sources on the methodology and source-corpus axes; agent 1 should expose agent 0's bias when a structurally correct diagram hides command-to-event causality, and agent 0 should expose agent 1's bias when an engaging trace obscures stable contracts, topology, or recursive composition.

Agent 0 optimizes exact architectural anatomy while agent 2 uses learner-task analysis, progressive disclosure, coordinated-view, and accessibility evidence on the methodology axis; agent 2 should expose agent 0's bias when notation is correct but cognitively overloaded, and agent 0 should expose agent 2's bias when simplification erases a type, invariant, or authority boundary.

Agent 1 optimizes event replay and state-transition comprehension while agent 2 optimizes orientation, focus, details-on-demand, and transfer across synchronized projections on the source-corpus and methodology axes; agent 2 should expose agent 1's bias when animation becomes transient spectacle, and agent 1 should expose agent 2's bias when a calm atlas fails to explain how one run actually advances, waits, gates, retries, and terminates.

agents.angle: Structural anatomy and notation: find the smallest view grammar that faithfully exposes the Work contract, recursive composition algebra, typed graph, component boundaries, and invariants.
agents.initial_prompt: Read the frozen DESIGN.md and ONTOLOGY.md identified by path and SHA-256 in strategy-inventory-packet.json. Treat them as candidate sources, not implemented truth. Research current primary or authoritative sources for software-architecture views and notations, including structural decomposition, component relationships, hierarchy, graph composition, and cross-view consistency; use direct official specifications or original research rather than secondary listicles. Compare at least three credible structural view grammars against this exact design. Produce a component-to-visual-encoding matrix covering WorkDefinition, WorkRun, leaf/composite substitutability, sequence, fan-out, fan-in, gate, sidecar, bounded repetition, explicit graph composition, root orchestrator, bus, journal, work units, commands, events, routing cursor, domain status, confirmation, effects, invariants, and residue. Test whether recursion should appear as nesting, type identity, graph expansion, or all three at different zoom levels. Return exact local selectors, external citations, benefits, failure modes, cognitive burden risks, and one recommended structural grammar. Explicitly identify what a structural diagram cannot explain alone. Do not edit files, design an implementation stack, equate the bus with decision authority, or imply nested independent orchestrators.

agents.angle: Temporal and causal trace: determine how commands, events, gates, retries, sidecars, derived routing state, and work-owned status should be replayed so a reader understands one execution.
agents.initial_prompt: Read the frozen target files and Inventory packet. Research current primary standards, official documentation, and original papers for workflow sequence views, event-driven systems, state machines, distributed traces, and animated or replayable transitions. Compare at least three temporal view grammars for this design. Build paper-executable traces for: (1) sequence with a gate; (2) fan-out followed by fan-in; and (3) a main work with a non-controlling sidecar plus one bounded retry. For every trace step, name the command or event, producer, consumer, correlation and causation identity, persisted fact, derived routing cursor, domain status owner, confirmation owner, and whether an external effect is permitted. Identify required timeline lanes, stable selections shared with other views, replay controls, and how to display duplicate, delayed, out-of-order, or terminal events without claiming observed runtime behavior. Return exact local selectors, external citations, view candidates, trade-offs, misleading animations to reject, and one recommended causal grammar. Explicitly identify what an event trace cannot explain alone. Do not edit files, invent runtime evidence, turn the journal into an executor, or let transport order substitute for causal semantics.

agents.angle: Learner-centered coordinated views: determine the navigation, progressive disclosure, comparison, and inspection pattern that helps both a novice and an expert understand every part without duplicating semantic truth.
agents.initial_prompt: Read the target files and the selected Inventory precedents, then verify any load-bearing local claim against its source artifact. Research primary information-visualization, human-computer interaction, learning-science, and accessibility sources for overview-plus-detail, coordinated multiple views, progressive disclosure, graph comprehension, animation, diagrams, and explanatory interaction. Derive two learner journeys: a novice asking 'what is this system and who owns what?' and an expert asking 'how does this concrete composite run and recover?'. Compare at least three interaction architectures, including the working hypothesis of synchronized Structure, Flow, and Ownership views. Require one immutable semantic source, stable cross-view selection, a part inspector, scenario playback, a text/table equivalent, keyboard-accessible navigation, visible claim ceilings, and a way to distinguish proposed from implemented behavior. Map all 16 DESIGN.md sections and all 14 ONTOLOGY.md sections to an overview, focused view, inspector card, scenario, or boundary notice so no part disappears. Return exact local selectors, external citations, comprehension hypotheses, measurable but not yet executed acceptance tasks, accessibility risks, and one recommended learner interaction grammar. Do not claim human comprehension, treat browser checks as learning proof, or create learner edges that alter semantic bytes.

Reconcile the three explorer returns without defaulting to their shared vocabulary. Compare the candidate view grammars against explicit criteria: coverage of every part, preservation of type and authority distinctions, explanation of causal execution, orientation cost, progressive disclosure, static and non-visual equivalence, exact source traceability, and honest proof ceiling. Produce: (1) a candidate comparison table; (2) one recommended primary view architecture with a compact wireframe; (3) synchronized Structure, Flow, Ownership, and Inspector responsibilities if supported, or a clearly better alternative if the hypothesis fails; (4) an exact mapping of all named design elements and ontology clusters to visible encodings; (5) the three finite scenario traces; (6) novice and expert paths; (7) one semantic-source and removable-projection contract; (8) negative controls for ownership collapse, recursion misrepresentation, timeline spectacle, graph overload, and status inflation; (9) an MVP versus later-capability boundary; (10) browser, accessibility, and human-comprehension validation plans kept separate; and (11) KILL, MERGE, or DEFER dispositions for losing candidates. Every load-bearing recommendation must cite an exact local selector and a direct external source, label evidence scope and uncertainty, and preserve proposal-only status. Do not write repository files.

groups.anti_bias: Attack-vector axis: precedent and ownership, finite explanatory non-vacuity, and definitional plus authority non-collapse.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 attacks duplication and unsupported novelty through existing local and external precedents while agent 1 attacks decorative explanation through finite tasks and counterexamples on the attack-vector axis; agent 1 should expose agent 0's bias when precedent reuse still cannot explain a run, and agent 0 should expose agent 1's bias when a bespoke demo reimplements a view or projection already owned.

Agent 0 classifies view patterns and owner boundaries while agent 2 attacks semantic and authority collapse on the attack-vector axis; agent 2 should expose agent 0's bias when an existing pattern is reused with the wrong meaning, and agent 0 should expose agent 2's bias when terminology objections ignore a proven removable projection pattern.

Agent 1 requires observable success and failure on concrete scenarios while agent 2 requires each visual distinction to preserve a distinct invariant and owner on the attack-vector axis; agent 2 should expose agent 1's bias when a persuasive scenario teaches a false ownership model, and agent 1 should expose agent 2's bias when perfectly separated categories do not help a reader answer any concrete question.

agents.angle: Precedent gate: verify direct sources, classify reuse versus invention, and prevent the recommendation from duplicating an owned local view or misusing an external notation.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply only the precedent and ownership gate to the synthesis. Verify local Inventory leads against their source artifacts and verify external claims against direct sources. Classify every recommended view primitive as already owned locally, build-from-owned, external-pattern reuse, or net-new candidate. Check whether graph/outline/table synchronization, learner projections, focus scenes, architecture notation, event timelines, state diagrams, and ownership matrices already have exact contracts that should be reused. Being owned never automatically emits KILL; instead state the reuse and authority consequence. Reject novelty claims based only on Inventory no-match, secondary summaries, or superficial naming similarity. Return PASS or a bounded revision with exact sources, owner, proof ceiling, and forbidden transfer.

agents.angle: Non-vacuity gate: force the recommendation to help a reader answer discriminating questions across concrete pipelines and to fail visibly when a view hides or misstates a part.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply only the non-vacuity and counterexample gate. Walk the proposed view by hand through the three required scenarios: gated sequence, fan-out/fan-in, and sidecar plus bounded retry. Require it to answer at least: what is a Work, why a pipeline is also Work, who may advance routing, who owns domain status, who owns confirmation, what the bus and journal do not do, what a gate controls, what a sidecar cannot control, how recursion terminates, and what happens on duplicate or delayed events. Add mutants that remove the ownership view, merge command and event lanes, render a composite as a nested orchestrator, color status without naming its owner, animate without a stable trace, and show an unbounded loop. KILL any view element that changes no answer and any recommendation that cannot distinguish the mutants. Return PASS or exact repairs plus a finite acceptance-task table; do not claim the tasks were user-tested.

agents.angle: Definitional and authority gate: ensure the visual language does not collapse Work with WorkRun, composition with authority, event with status, journal with executor, or projection with source truth.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply only the definitional-soundness and authority non-collapse gate. Inspect every visual entity, relation, lane, state, color, animation, and interaction for a distinct meaning and failure mode. Specifically test WorkDefinition versus WorkRun; leaf versus composite substitutability; recursive composition versus recursive orchestration authority; command versus event; transport versus persistence versus decision versus execution; routing cursor versus domain status; acceptance status versus confirmation; gate decision versus external effect permission; main branch versus sidecar; structural edge versus temporal occurrence; and source semantics versus learner projection. Require a legend, owner label, claim-ceiling label, and misuse warning where visual similarity could mislead. Return KEEP, MERGE, RENAME, DEFER, or KILL decisions and PASS only if the smallest repaired vocabulary remains understandable.

Write findings.md only from the evidence-closed synthesis and reviewer receipts. Lead with the recommended view architecture in plain language, then show a compact text wireframe and the one-image overview. Explain why it won over the alternatives. Include a part-by-part atlas that accounts for every DESIGN.md and ONTOLOGY.md section; exact visual grammar and legend; the synchronized-view contract; three scenario walkthroughs; novice and expert journeys; stable selection and inspector behavior; static, table, keyboard, and reduced-motion equivalents; ownership and claim-ceiling boundaries; MVP versus later work; negative controls; separated browser, accessibility, agent-structural, and human-comprehension validation plans; direct source trace; unresolved residue; and a research verdict matrix with precedent, non-vacuity, and definitional verdicts. State clearly that the artifact is a research recommendation, not an implemented or human-validated view. Write no HTML, JSON model, ontology, design edits, Inventory, ledger, Git, publication, promotion, release, deployment, or runtime claim.

Audit findings.md only against the frozen goal, exact-binding evidence contract, reviewer verdicts, and source packet. Require one unambiguous primary recommendation; explicit comparison with rejected alternatives; complete coverage of all design and ontology parts; faithful Work/WorkRun, recursion, composition, command/event, bus/journal, ownership, gate, sidecar, retry, failure, and claim-ceiling semantics; three finite walkthroughs; source-backed view decisions; stable coordinated-view and non-visual-equivalent contracts; separate browser, accessibility, agent-structural, and human-comprehension proof ceilings; and no invented runtime observation or promotion. Reject a beautiful but semantically lossy diagram, an inventory dump, a view collection without one primary organizing grammar, unsupported external claims, or missing exact selectors. Return ACCEPT or one bounded writer revision list.
